name: ATtiny85
description: 8-pin 8-bit AVR RISC microcontroller with 8 KB flash, 512 B SRAM and 512 B EEPROM. In DIP-8/SOIC-8 it exposes just 6 GPIO yet still offers a 10-bit ADC, two timers (one with a high-speed PLL for fast PWM), a USI for SPI/I2C, and internal 8/16 MHz oscillators needing no external crystal. A hobbyist favorite for tiny battery projects and the brain of the Digispark, because it is cheap, breadboard-friendly and Arduino-programmable. Standout feature: the on-chip 64 MHz PLL feeding Timer1 for high-resolution PWM from an 8-pin part.

pins.name: PB5
pins.description: GPIO PB5; doubles as RESET (active-low), ADC0, dW (debugWIRE), PCINT5

pins.name: PB3
pins.description: GPIO PB3; XTAL1/CLKI crystal/clock input, ADC3, PCINT3

pins.name: PB4
pins.description: GPIO PB4; XTAL2/CLKO crystal/clock output, ADC2, PCINT4

pins.name: PB0
pins.description: GPIO PB0; MOSI/DI, SDA (USI), AIN0, OC0A, OC1A, AREF, PCINT0

pins.name: PB1
pins.description: GPIO PB1; MISO/DO, AIN1, OC0B, OC1A, PCINT1

pins.name: PB2
pins.description: GPIO PB2; SCK/USCK, SCL (USI), ADC1, T0, INT0, PCINT2

extra.timers: two 8-bit; Timer1 with 64 MHz PLL clock option

typical_application: Compact battery-powered sensors, LED/PWM controllers, and Digispark-style USB dongles where a full Arduino is overkill.
gotchas: pin 1 RESET is shared with PB5; using it as a normal GPIO requires fuse-disabling RESET, which then needs a high-voltage (12 V) programmer to recover
only 6 usable GPIO and they multiplex ADC, SPI, PWM and clock pins, so peripheral choices conflict quickly
no hardware UART; serial relies on USI or software bit-banging
default fuse runs the internal RC oscillator at 1 MHz (CKDIV8 set), so it appears 8x slow until you clear CKDIV8
ATtiny85 vs ATtiny85V are different speed/voltage grades; the plain part is not rated below 2.7 V at full clock
USI is not a true I2C/SPI peripheral, so protocols need a software state machine
